quests.hint: The paper showing how much you owe after a meal.
quests.explanation: In a restaurant we ask for 'the bill' (British) or 'the check' (American). Both are polite, and 'bill' is the standard choice in international English.
quests.textToSpeak: Excuse me, could we have the ___, please? We're ready to pay.
quests.correctAnswer: Excuse me, could we have the bill, please? We're ready to pay.
quests.contextClue: 'Ready to pay' shows the meal is finished.

quests.hint: Your body reacts badly to something you eat or touch.
quests.explanation: We say 'allergic to' + the thing: 'allergic to peanuts', 'allergic to cats'. The noun is 'allergy': 'I have a nut allergy'.
quests.textToSpeak: I'm ___ to peanuts, so please make sure there are none in the sauce.
quests.correctAnswer: I'm allergic to peanuts, so please make sure there are none in the sauce.
quests.contextClue: Asking that an ingredient be left out signals a health problem.

quests.hint: The list of dishes a restaurant serves.
quests.explanation: In a restaurant we ask for 'the menu' first. The word is also used for the list of options on a screen or in an app.
quests.textToSpeak: Can I see the ___, please? I haven't decided what to order yet.
quests.correctAnswer: Can I see the menu, please? I haven't decided what to order yet.
quests.contextClue: Not knowing what to order calls for a list of choices.

quests.hint: Looking around a shop without buying anything yet.
quests.explanation: 'Just browsing' is the polite reply when a shop assistant asks if you need help. The verb 'browse' also applies to websites.
quests.textToSpeak: I'm just ___, thanks. I'll let you know if I need any help.
quests.correctAnswer: I'm just browsing, thanks. I'll let you know if I need any help.
quests.contextClue: Politely declining help suggests no specific purchase yet.

quests.hint: Give it back and take a different one instead.
quests.explanation: 'Exchange X for Y' means to swap one item for another. It differs from a refund, where you get your money back.
quests.textToSpeak: This sweater doesn't fit. Can I ___ it for a smaller one?
quests.correctAnswer: This sweater doesn't fit. Can I exchange it for a smaller one?
quests.contextClue: The reason (it doesn't fit) and 'a smaller one' show a swap.

quests.hint: The past form of 'sell'.
quests.explanation: 'Sold out' means no more are available: 'The tickets are sold out'. The past participle of sell is 'sold'.
quests.textToSpeak: Do you still have this jacket in black? The website says it's ___ out.
quests.correctAnswer: Do you still have this jacket in black? The website says it's sold out.
quests.contextClue: A website reporting no stock explains the question.

quests.hint: Come to a halt to let passengers on or off.
quests.explanation: We use 'stop at' for a route: 'This train stops at Reading.' 'Go to' describes the final destination.
quests.textToSpeak: Excuse me, does this bus ___ at the airport?
quests.correctAnswer: Excuse me, does this bus stop at the airport?
quests.contextClue: The passenger is checking whether the route includes the airport.

quests.hint: The empty space between two things.
quests.explanation: 'Mind the gap' is a well-known warning in British train and metro stations. 'Mind' here means be careful about.
quests.textToSpeak: Please mind the ___ when you step off the train.
quests.correctAnswer: Please mind the gap when you step off the train.
quests.contextClue: A warning about stepping off a train points to a space.

quests.hint: The price you pay for a journey on a bus or train.
quests.explanation: 'Fare' is the cost of a journey. We use 'fee' for a service and 'price' for goods, so we say 'bus fare' and 'train fare'.
quests.textToSpeak: How much is the ___ to the city centre? I only have coins.
quests.correctAnswer: How much is the fare to the city centre? I only have coins.
quests.contextClue: The cost of getting somewhere is being asked about.

quests.hint: Across from; facing.
quests.explanation: As a preposition, 'opposite' means facing something across a space: 'opposite the station'. American English often says 'across from'.
quests.textToSpeak: The bank is ___ the supermarket, on the other side of the road.
quests.correctAnswer: The bank is opposite the supermarket, on the other side of the road.
quests.contextClue: 'The other side of the road' explains the position.

quests.hint: A circular junction where cars go round to reach their exit.
quests.explanation: A roundabout is a circular junction where you follow the circle to your exit. Americans may say 'traffic circle'.
quests.textToSpeak: Keep driving until you reach the ___, then take the second exit for the airport.
quests.correctAnswer: Keep driving until you reach the roundabout, then take the second exit for the airport.
quests.contextClue: 'Take the second exit' matches a circular junction.

quests.hint: Moving on foot.
quests.explanation: For travel time we say 'a ten-minute walk' or 'a ten-minute drive'. In that phrase, 'minute' stays singular and takes a hyphen.
quests.textToSpeak: It's about a ten-minute ___ from here, so you don't need a taxi.
quests.correctAnswer: It's about a ten-minute walk from here, so you don't need a taxi.
quests.contextClue: Not needing a taxi shows the distance is short.

quests.hint: Move an arranged meeting to a new time.
quests.explanation: 'Reschedule' means to move something to a new time. 'Postpone' means to delay it, and 'cancel' means to end it.
quests.textToSpeak: I'm afraid I can't make Thursday. Could we ___ for the following week?
quests.correctAnswer: I'm afraid I can't make Thursday. Could we reschedule for the following week?
quests.contextClue: Being unable to attend on Thursday leads to a request for a new date.

quests.hint: A recorded message you leave when someone doesn't pick up.
quests.explanation: We 'leave a message' on someone's voicemail. 'Leave a voicemail' also works.
quests.textToSpeak: He isn't answering, so I left a message on his ___.
quests.correctAnswer: He isn't answering, so I left a message on his voicemail.
quests.contextClue: No answer means a recording is the only option.

quests.hint: The small word that introduces the topic.
quests.explanation: 'Call about' + topic gives the reason for a call: 'I'm calling about the job'. Formal writing often uses 'regarding'.
quests.textToSpeak: Hello, I'm calling ___ the job advertised on your website.
quests.correctAnswer: Hello, I'm calling about the job advertised on your website.
quests.contextClue: The job advert is the subject of the call.

quests.hint: Reached its destination.
quests.explanation: 'Hasn't arrived' uses the present perfect for something still expected. We arrive 'in' a city and 'at' a smaller place.
quests.textToSpeak: My parcel was due on Monday, but it still hasn't ___.
quests.correctAnswer: My parcel was due on Monday, but it still hasn't arrived.
quests.contextClue: 'Due on Monday' and 'still' show the delay.

quests.hint: A formal way of saying you are unhappy about something.
quests.explanation: We 'make a complaint' or 'complain about' something. The noun is 'complaint' and the verb is 'complain'.
quests.textToSpeak: I'd like to make a ___ about the service; we waited an hour for our food.
quests.correctAnswer: I'd like to make a complaint about the service; we waited an hour for our food.
quests.contextClue: An hour's wait is the reason the speaker is dissatisfied.

quests.hint: Harmed so that it no longer looks or works properly.
quests.explanation: Use 'damaged' for something harmed but not necessarily destroyed. 'Broken' suggests it no longer works or has come apart.
quests.textToSpeak: The item was ___ when I opened the box: the screen has a crack across it.
quests.correctAnswer: The item was damaged when I opened the box: the screen has a crack across it.
quests.contextClue: A crack across the screen is the evidence.

quests.hint: Not busy; with no plans.
quests.explanation: 'Are you free?' asks whether someone has no plans. It is friendly and natural. 'Available' is more formal, used mainly in work contexts.
quests.textToSpeak: Are you ___ on Friday evening? A few of us are going bowling.
quests.correctAnswer: Are you free on Friday evening? A few of us are going bowling.
quests.contextClue: The invitation depends on their schedule.

quests.hint: A polite word for suitable and easy for you.
quests.explanation: 'Convenient' is a polite way to check whether a time suits someone: 'Is this time convenient?' In casual talk we say 'Does that work for you?'
quests.textToSpeak: Would Thursday afternoon be ___ for you?
quests.correctAnswer: Would Thursday afternoon be convenient for you?
quests.contextClue: A specific day is offered, and the speaker checks that it fits.

quests.hint: At a time that hasn't been decided yet.
quests.explanation: 'Sometime' (one word) means at an unspecified time: 'sometime next week'. 'Some time' (two words) means an amount of time: 'It will take some time'.
quests.textToSpeak: Let's get together for coffee ___ next week.
quests.correctAnswer: Let's get together for coffee sometime next week.
quests.contextClue: The plan has no fixed day or hour.

quests.hint: Demonstrate so I can see it done.
quests.explanation: 'Show me how to...' or 'show me how it works' asks for a demonstration. It suggests you will watch, not just hear an explanation.
quests.textToSpeak: This ticket machine confuses me. Can someone ___ me how it works?
quests.correctAnswer: This ticket machine confuses me. Can someone show me how it works?
quests.contextClue: Being confused by a machine leads to a request for a demonstration.

quests.hint: The part that stores power.
quests.explanation: We say a battery is 'dead' or 'flat' when it has no power. 'Flat' is common in British English, and 'dead' works in both.
quests.textToSpeak: My phone won't turn on. I think the ___ is dead.
quests.correctAnswer: My phone won't turn on. I think the battery is dead.
quests.contextClue: A phone that won't turn on suggests a lack of power.

quests.hint: Use your eyes to check something.
quests.explanation: 'Take a look at' something means to examine it: 'Could you take a look at my laptop?' British speakers also say 'have a look'.
quests.textToSpeak: The printer is jammed again. Could you take a ___ at it?
quests.correctAnswer: The printer is jammed again. Could you take a look at it?
quests.contextClue: A jammed printer needs someone to inspect it.

quests.hint: Twist the handle.
quests.explanation: We 'turn' taps on and off. For lights and machines we often use 'switch' as well: 'switch off the light'.
quests.textToSpeak: The tap has been dripping all night. I can't ___ it off properly.
quests.correctAnswer: The tap has been dripping all night. I can't turn it off properly.
quests.contextClue: A tap has a handle that must be twisted to stop the water.

quests.hint: A hole or crack that lets water or gas escape.
quests.explanation: A leak is a small hole or crack where liquid or gas escapes: 'a gas leak', 'a leak in the roof'. It is also a verb: 'the roof leaks'.
quests.textToSpeak: There's a ___ in the roof, and water comes in every time it rains.
quests.correctAnswer: There's a leak in the roof, and water comes in every time it rains.
quests.contextClue: Water coming in only when it rains points to a fault.

quests.hint: The opposite of in.
quests.explanation: 'Lock yourself out (of)' means to be outside with no way to get back in. Related: 'locked in'.
quests.textToSpeak: I locked myself ___ of the flat, so I had to call a locksmith.
quests.correctAnswer: I locked myself out of the flat, so I had to call a locksmith.
quests.contextClue: Calling a locksmith shows the speaker couldn't get inside.

quests.hint: Money that is paid back to you.
quests.explanation: A refund is money paid back. We 'ask for', 'get' or 'claim' a refund, often 'a refund on' something.
quests.textToSpeak: The concert was cancelled, so I'm waiting for a ___ on my ticket.
quests.correctAnswer: The concert was cancelled, so I'm waiting for a refund on my ticket.
quests.contextClue: A cancelled event means the payment should come back.

quests.hint: The small word that follows 'apologise' before the reason.
quests.explanation: 'Apologise for' + reason, and 'apologise to' + person: 'We apologise to passengers for the delay.'
quests.textToSpeak: We apologise ___ the delay and appreciate your patience.
quests.correctAnswer: We apologise for the delay and appreciate your patience.
quests.contextClue: An announcement like this names what caused the wait.

quests.hint: Watch something carefully.
quests.explanation: 'Keep an eye on' something means watch and look after it. 'Keep an eye out for' means watch for something to appear.
quests.textToSpeak: I'm just popping to the toilet. Would you keep an ___ on my bag?
quests.correctAnswer: I'm just popping to the toilet. Would you keep an eye on my bag?
quests.contextClue: Leaving a bag briefly needs someone to watch it.
